section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the relationship between external shame, self-compassion, and body appreciation in young male and female adults. The study used path analysis to test whether self-compassion mediates the relationship between external shame and body appreciation (positive body image), finding significant direct and indirect effects of shame on body appreciation through self-compassion for both sexes. The authors acknowledge methodological limitations including the cross-sectional design, small sample size, use of self-report measures, and lack of counterbalanced design, while suggesting future research should include clinical samples and explore additional variables such as internal shame.
